_reviewer_calls._what_this_is: JSON carries no comments, and four fields below are NOT in the human's source blueprint — they are reviewer calls made to translate that source into the shape `Blueprint` parses. Recorded here, beside the fields themselves, for the human to confirm or override. Ignored by the parser (pydantic drops unknown keys); it is documentation, not contract.
_reviewer_calls.duration_minutes: NOT IN SOURCE. 180 minutes chosen to match the house convention: final_default.json is also 100 marks / 180 minutes. Confirm.
_reviewer_calls.item_type: NOT IN SOURCE, and load-bearing — `item_type` decides which validation gates apply. TRUE_FALSE_SERIES -> mcq with options_count 2, so gate 4 (MCQ hygiene) still applies and passes: 'True'/'False' sit inside the +/-40% OPTION_LENGTH_BAND and neither is an 'all of the above'. ALGORITHMIC_TRACE_PROBLEM / SCENARIO_MODELING_AND_SOLVING / MATHEMATICAL_MODELING -> long. ANALYTICAL_SHORT_ANSWER -> short. Confirm.
_reviewer_calls.grounding: NOT IN SOURCE, and it decides whether gate 2 runs at all. Read from each task's own instructions: q1 'testing theoretical properties' -> span; q2 'Generate a novel adversarial game tree' -> synthesis; q3 'Generate a novel word problem' -> synthesis; q4 'Define a state-space environment' -> synthesis; q5 'Present the mathematical update rules' (the rules come from the material) -> span. That is 8 of 20 items synthesis = 40%, above SYNTHESIS_ITEM_WARN_RATIO = 0.25, so the manifest WILL warn on this blueprint. That is correct behaviour and must not be silenced: nearly half this paper is not answerable from the student's own slides, and saying so out loud is the whole point of stage 3. Confirm.
_reviewer_calls.bloom: NOT A TRANSLATION. The source's compound labels (REMEMBER_UNDERSTAND, APPLY_ANALYZE, EVALUATE) are carried through unchanged rather than mapped onto the lowercase single-level scheme the three shipped blueprints use. `bloom` is list[str] with no fixed vocabulary, and the realised distribution must use the SAME labels as `cognitive_balance` or the declared-vs-realised comparison in CoverageReport compares nothing. Confirm.
_reviewer_calls.known_consequence: cognitive_balance is a MARKS mix in the source (20/70/10 of 100 marks) but CoverageReport.bloom_realised is an ITEMS mix (10/8/2 of 20 items = 0.50/0.40/0.10). The two can never agree for this blueprint, so a fully-filled paper still raises two COGNITIVE_BALANCE_TOLERANCE warnings. Not a bug in either field; left for the human to decide.

sections.title: True/False: Search Algorithms
sections.topic: Uninformed and Informed Search (BFS, DFS, A*, Heuristics)
sections.generation_instructions: Generate 10 True/False statements testing theoretical properties of search algorithms, such as admissibility, optimality, and node expansion comparisons.

sections.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning Trace
sections.topic: Adversarial Search and Minimax with Alpha-Beta Pruning
sections.generation_instructions: Generate a novel adversarial game tree graph with terminal leaf values. Ask the student to trace the Alpha-Beta pruning algorithm, explicitly requiring them to show pruned branches and propagated node values.

sections.title: Constraint Satisfaction Modelling
sections.generation_instructions: Generate a novel word problem with entities and constraints. Sub-questions must require: 1) Defining variables and initial domains. 2) Applying MRV heuristic. 3) Executing a two-pass domain pruning and assignment algorithm.

sections.title: Markov Decision Process Modelling
sections.generation_instructions: Define a state-space environment with transition models and rewards. Sub-questions must require: 1) Formulating Bellman equations. 2) Executing manual policy extraction/value iteration for specific states. 3) Evaluating the optimality of a given mock policy.

sections.title: Reinforcement Learning Comparison
sections.generation_instructions: Present the mathematical update rules for two RL algorithms (e.g., Q-learning and SARSA). Ask the student to evaluate and compare their convergence properties under a specific exploratory policy scenario.
